Sources & data notes

BiblePath combines its original 157 curated profiles with a broad, disambiguated base index of people from the Old and New Testaments, plus independently sourced Catholic supplemental profiles. This is an expanding research collection, not a claim that every person, interpretation or family relationship has been captured.

Roman Catholic focus and current coverage

The Christian account in the people comparison follows a Roman Catholic perspective, with biblical passages and separately identified references to the Catechism of the Catholic Church and Church teaching. Jewish and Islamic accounts retain their own sources and identities.

The Dutch Catholic collection and English Douay-Rheims 1899 each contain the Catholic canon of 73 books: 46 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New (Catechism §120). It includes Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, 1 and 2 Maccabees, and the Greek additions to Esther and Daniel. Catholic supplemental person profiles retain their reviewed English Douay-Rheims citations; their primary reading action opens the reviewed Dutch counterpart and a separate source link preserves the original citation. The original 2,987-person family graph and 604-city atlas retain their source scope of 66 shared books; the people collection is not an exhaustive concordance. The existing World English Bible, Statenvertaling and Louis Segond editions remain separate 66-book editions, not complete Catholic translations. Dutch is the first-visit default for both interface and Catholic scripture. The Dutch collection uses Canisius 1939 with explicitly sourced historical Catholic supplements for gaps in the digital transcription. Previously saved language and edition choices are preserved.

STEP Bible

The base atlas’s identity and genealogy data was created for STEP Bible, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge, and is used under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license.

The authoritative source is STEPBible/STEPBible-Data, specifically TIPNR — Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References. This build is pinned to commit ed476a8ee6e3f7b3a46fc48af6c7dabc02387b1d, retrieved on 21 October 2026. Individual profile and relationship sources link to the corresponding record in that snapshot.

Changes to the STEP base index

  • Selected named or title-identified human records. Place, group, deity, ambiguous person-or-town, synthetic anonymous bridge, historical-name-only and LXX-only records are omitted. References are restricted to the 66-book Protestant canon.
  • Preserved distinct identities for people with the same name. The original 157 BiblePath IDs and summaries are retained through an explicit, reviewed mapping.
  • Converted structured roles, names, parent and partner fields to the app format. New short descriptions use these structured fields. The source’s AI-generated Brief, Short and Article biographies are not imported.
  • Normalized biblical reference notation and linked imported name references to the ESV on Bible Gateway. Original curated passages retain their KJV links. The reader identifies each translation separately; these legacy source locators are not silently reassigned to the Catholic edition.
  • Omitted group/form word entries and LXX-only references. Some retained source name references can still concern a nation, descendant group, or another use of an ancestral name. They are presented as name references from the index, not independently verified quotations about the individual.
  • Omitted uncertain, indirect-ancestor, founder and descendant-group claims from direct parent lines. A flag in either the forward or reverse record suppresses the imported relationship.
  • Kept original verse-backed links and their notes. Added index-derived links with an explicit STEP Bible relationship-index citation, rather than presenting an arbitrary name reference as proof of a family relationship.
  • Corrected Lappidoth’s upstream gender field using Judges 4:4, and Deborah of Genesis 35:8’s role to Rebekah’s nurse. These corrections are annotated in their profiles and in scripts/person-overrides.json.
  • Omitted the source’s disputed Nahash identity from 2 Samuel 17:25, pending review. That verse names Nahash as Abigail’s parent, but does not establish the source’s identification of Nahash as Jesse’s wife and mother of his sons. Ten unsupported links are therefore omitted; the other three Nahash identities remain available.

Care with genealogies

Joseph’s relationship to Jesus remains explicitly legal parenthood. Heli is not assigned as Mary’s biological father. Disputed biological-parent interpretations for Jesus’ brethren, unproven spouse relationships, and selected ambiguous genealogical harmonizations are omitted. A missing line may therefore mean uncertainty or an import limitation rather than an absence of biblical evidence.

STEP Bible’s interpretation choices are useful research aids, but are not themselves the biblical text. Please follow the source links and compare the cited passages. The app distinguishes original passage-backed connections from imported index connections.

The Dutch Catholic collection

The first-visit default contains all 73 Catholic books, 1,334 chapters and 35,510 verse records in Dutch. It is based on the Petrus Canisius translation of 1939. The eBible export omits Greek Esther additions and the prayer/song in Daniel 3. The pinned original Canisius OSIS supplies Esther 10:4–15, except 15:1, and the complete book of Daniel. Daniel is taken as a whole to preserve its chapter 3/4 boundary without duplicated text. Esther 15:1 and 16:1–24, absent from both electronic sources, use the historical Catholic translation by J. M. van Oers in the unchanged second edition of 1933, transcribed from DBNL. These 25 verses have individual source notes and links in the reader. This is an explicitly documented composite reading edition; no scripture wording is machine-translated or generated.

Historical spelling, punctuation and source numbering are retained; whitespace is normalized. The seven deuterocanonical books, all Greek Esther and Daniel additions, and the Letter of Jeremiah (Baruch 6) are included. Psalm 84:9–10 is a single source verse bridge: either number opens the same text, which is displayed and searched once. Textual variants, source notes and nonconsecutive verse numbers remain visible. Canisius is identified as public domain by eBible; the original OSIS transcription is CC0. Van Oers died in 1945; the original historical translation is public domain. Sources, rights evidence, checksums and the supplement transcription are recorded in the importer and dataset.

  • Canisius 1939 · eBible USFX · Public domain · SHA-256: 08d8647b5bd0fc9cdf5043aadabc904fb165cb2575b0f369afd64ea3f695abc8
  • Canisius · OSIS · CC0-1.0 · commit 70838411d24086ccb5761712af4949604a390e4a · SHA-256: 9742d2fd460155af9e7eeb21719badfe8965ae8cc40219e960840edf682cc712
  • J. M. van Oers · De heilige boeken van het oude verbond, deel 3 (1933) · Public domain · SHA-256: 01575cf327d5ef887c9909f0a0803256c64836797b18ed1d280750b21cb01951

python scripts/import-catholic-dutch.py --check reproduces the collection. The tests independently compare the imported text with its source components. English Catholic person citations retain their reviewed Douay-Rheims coordinates. Equal verse numbers in the Dutch collection do not establish alignment with Douay-Rheims or the original atlas.

Person passage navigation

Bible person profiles open the Dutch Catholic reader through a separately reviewed passage map. The map preserves each source citation and translates only its coordinates. The reader displays source and target references, highlights the full target range and offers separate buttons for split or reordered passages. Textual variants and partial correspondences are explained. Unknown source editions and unreviewed references never inherit identical verse numbers as a guess; the original source remains available. This is navigation evidence, not a new assertion of person identity or genealogy. Torah, Qur’an and city references keep their existing source context.

node scripts/build-person-passage-map.cjs --check reproduces the map from its pinned scripture inputs and reviewed rules. Tests validate every published person reference, source-edition isolation, target existence, changed numbering, split passages and failed-load recovery.

The passage map covers all 20,707 source-reference occurrences (11,443 edition-specific references; 19 partial correspondences). Numbering evidence includes STEP TVTMS, STEPBible.org, Tyndale House, Cambridge, under CC BY 4.0. Adaptations select and invert applicable conditional numbering rules and add direct Canisius/Douay–Rheims passage reviews. Original citations remain unchanged.

The English Catholic edition

The reader includes the Douay-Rheims American Edition of 1899, translated from the Latin Vulgate into English: 73 books, 1,334 chapters and 35,811 numbered verses. The source publisher identifies this text as public domain. The official USFX download was retrieved on 22 October 2026; SHA-256: def7a79a4fd11a9489ea7d25579658b70f0727a8dcf7f71c3ca1c9e5cca2d5db. Wording, punctuation and every numbered verse are preserved, with documented whitespace normalization. This complete translation is not assembled from passages in different editions.

The source’s Vulgate numbering is retained, including Esther 10:4–16:24, the Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three in Daniel 3:24–90, Susanna in Daniel 13, Bel and the Dragon in Daniel 14, and the Letter of Jeremiah in Baruch 6. Modern book labels aid navigation without changing the source text. Equal verse numbers are not assumed to align with WEB or other translations: legacy atlas name candidates remain uncertain across the shared books. Catholic supplemental profiles contain original editorial summaries and edition-specific passage references; no new family relationships are inferred. Existing comparison panels retain their WEB locators, and Catholic doctrinal sources remain separately identified.

The existing World English Bible edition

The reader also contains the 66-book Protestant edition of the World English Bible in American English: 1,189 chapters and 31,103 numbered verses. The text is public domain. World English Bible is a trademark of eBible.org. The official USFX source was retrieved on 22 October 2026; its SHA-256 is 6b95cc0f7207fe2a1805370d4db6121bbcdf809ec8609a8a3d91f063214a911b.

Verse wording and punctuation are retained, with whitespace normalized. Psalm superscriptions, speaker headings and source footnotes are preserved separately. Prefaces, cross-reference lists, word-tag metadata and books outside the bundled 66-book edition are omitted. Some numbered verses have no main text in this edition; their source notes explain the textual variation.

Name links are BiblePath annotations, not part of the translation. They match names and aliases against the identity index, prioritizing identities indexed at that exact verse only where edition numbering is aligned. Namesakes, possible name-only matches and collective names such as Israel are marked as ambiguous and offer a choice. A name link is a research aid, not a guarantee that every use refers to the selected individual. Spelling differences or missing index entries can leave a name unlinked.

Dutch and French editions

The bundled 66-book Dutch Statenvertaling (1888 transcription by Isidore-Guild, CC0) and French Louis Segond 1910 (eBible.org, public domain) remain available. These are distinct from the complete Dutch and English Catholic collections; changing interface language does not translate scripture. Each edition preserves its own text and verse numbering; source footnotes for these editions are omitted. Numbering differences in French books are treated conservatively: name matches offer possible identities rather than claiming an exact-verse identification. Translated profiles use conventional local names while retaining original aliases and stable IDs. Source downloads, checksums, and processing details are recorded in each dataset and the multilingual importer.

Cities and towns

The cities explorer contains 604 named settlements with 4,125 indexed verse references from the original 66-book atlas. STEP Bible supplies the identities, name forms and biblical references. Settlement classification comes from OpenBible.info’s Bible geography data, licensed under CC BY 4.0, pinned to commit 7eb18a5ee62f27b9b93bd6689ea272d76dd23b8f. Individual records link to their source evidence. We selected and reformatted settlements, generated brief descriptions from structured reference fields, and omitted countries, rivers, mountains and ambiguous classifications. We did not import modern coordinates or source AI biographies.

Indexed city names can include poetic, regional and symbolic uses. Same-named or source-combined settlements carry notes where available. People listed beside a city are indexed in the same verses; that alone does not establish residence or physical presence. No endorsement by OpenBible.info is implied.

Connecting two people

The finder searches people with family links in the original base atlas. It first looks for a directed ancestral route, then a reverse ancestral route, and then a shortest family route. Among equally short routes, it prefers more Bible-cited connections. The default searches only links with explicit biblical citations. Disabling that filter admits clearly labeled STEP-indexed links. Every displayed step retains its original source and notes. A missing route is an index limitation, not proof that two people are unrelated.

The Adam-to-Jesus example has 63 steps, combines the atlas’s selected genealogy accounts, and includes Joseph’s legal parenthood. It is not a claim to reproduce Luke’s genealogy or an uninterrupted biological lineage. Genealogy lists can omit generations.

Reproducibility

The local project includes scripts/import-tipnr.cjs, scripts/import-bible.py, scripts/import-catholic-bible.py, scripts/import-catholic-dutch.py, scripts/import-places.cjs, original curated data, explicit identity mappings, exclusions, source checksums, and validation checks. The importers regenerate the deployable data files. Unmodified downloads are kept in an ignored local cache. python scripts/import-catholic-bible.py --check reproduces the Catholic asset without modifying it; its importer test independently compares all 35,811 verse texts against the pinned source XML.

Credit: data from STEP Bible, CC BY 4.0; selected, reformatted and supplemented for BiblePath. Changes are documented above and in the import scripts. No endorsement by STEP Bible is implied.
